component: SPECTER experimental FSR2 2.2.1 luminance first-mip reference

researchedButNotImplemented.singlePassDownsampler: AMD SPD workgroup remapping, subgroup reductions, groupshared intermediates, mip-5 handoff, and global atomic last-workgroup continuation
researchedButNotImplemented.selectedShadingChangeMip: FSR2 2.2.1 selects SPD mip index 4 for shading-change detection
researchedButNotImplemented.autoExposure: exp(Lavg); S=100.0, K=12.5, ExposureISO100=log2((Lavg*S)/K), q=0.65, Lmax=(78.0/(q*S))*pow(2.0, ExposureISO100), exposure=1/Lmax
researchedButNotImplemented.remainingFsr2Passes: Reconstruct and dilate, depth clip, create locks, reproject and accumulate, and RCAS

deliberateDifferences: WGSL and WebGPU are not upstream AMD backends; this port was authored for an isolated SPECTER experiment.
The shader dispatches one invocation per half-resolution output instead of AMD SPD's 256-thread single-dispatch hierarchy.
It materializes only the first 2x2 reduction and does not generate AMD's selected mip index 4 or the 1x1 exposure result.
It writes R32_FLOAT reference staging output rather than claiming the production FSR2 R16_FLOAT current-luminance resource plan.
The JavaScript oracle uses IEEE-754 binary64 arithmetic, so GPU FP32 results are compared by tolerance rather than bit identity.
